name: Contraptions
pages: Create adds a new feature called {b}contraptions{/}. A contraption is a structure of blocks that is {!}"assembled"{/}, usually with {i}super glue{/}, converting the structure from a set of blocks into a single contraption entity.{pb}Contraptions make unique designs and clever mobile machinery possible.

There are several {b}anchors{/} that can be used to form different types of contraptions with different behaviors.{pb}{i}Mechanical pistons{/}, {i}sticky mechanical pistons{/}, {i}rope pulleys{/}, and {i}gantry carriages{/} can create {!}collision-based contraptions{/}, which move in a straight path. These types of contraptions can be stopped by obstacles in their path.

{i}Windmill bearings{/} or {i}mechanical bearings{/} can be used to make {!}radial contraptions{/}. These rotate in an arch or circle, rather than moving in a straight line, and can pass through solid blocks in their path.{pb}An {i}elevator pulley{/} can be used to make an {!}elevator contraption{/}. Elevators can also pass through solid blocks, but can be set with specific floors to stop at to easily get around your builds.

The {i}cart assembler{/} can be used to form a {!}minecart contraption{/} which can also pass through solid blocks. The {i}minecart{/} will follow any set of {i}rails{/}, but carrying the contraption with it.{pb}{i}Minecart contraptions{/} can also be picked up in your inventory using a {i}wrench{/}, meaning you can create portable structures, vehicles, and storage systems.

Lastly, there are {!}trains{/}. These are similar to {i}minecart contraptions{/}, but with more advanced functionality, such as following a {i}train schedule{/}, being driven by players, and transporting items from one {i}train station{/} to another. (Check out {l:transportation/trains/}this chapter{/l} for more information on trains!){pb}Remember that blocks assembled as a contraption don't always behave the same way as they do when disassembled.

Rotational power can't be used on a contraption, but many components will be powered by the movement of the contraption. The faster a contraption is moving, the faster any {i}drills{/}, {i}saws{/}, or {i}deployers{/} on it will work.{pb}{i}Redstone{/} components can't update while on an assembled contraption, nor can they power anything else (except for {i}redstone contacts{/}). And if you try to place or break a block on an assembled contraption, you'll click right through it.
